title: Trade blocs & globalisation
examples: What is the main difference between an FTA and a customs union?
How does the WTO affect smaller economies?
Can you give an example of a successful trade bloc?

explain.say: Today we are looking at trade blocs and globalisation in economics.

items: These concepts are interconnected in economics.

explain.say: First we will explore Free Trade Agreements or FTAs.
Next we look at Customs Unions, which are stronger agreements.
The World Trade Organization, or WTO, sets global trade rules.
In a simple FTA, say, two countries lower tariffs on each other's goods.

draw.text: FTA Example: Country A <-> Country B

explain.say: For a customs union, all members must use the same external tariff rate.

faq.q: What is the main difference between an FTA and a customs union?
faq.a: An FTA only reduces tariffs between members. A customs union requires all members to adopt a single common external tariff rate.
asks: How is a customs union stronger than an FTA?
Must all countries in a bloc have the same rules?

faq.q: Does joining a trade bloc always benefit a country?
faq.a: It can bring benefits like market access, but it might limit a country's ability to set its own trade policy.
asks: Are there disadvantages to joining a bloc?
Could a country lose sovereignty by joining?

faq.q: What is the role of the WTO in global trade?
faq.a: The WTO provides a forum for trade negotiations and acts to settle trade disputes between member nations.
asks: Does the WTO control all trade?
What happens if a country breaks WTO rules?

faq.q: What is globalisation in the context of trade?
faq.a: Globalisation means that economies become increasingly interconnected through the movement of goods, services, and capital across borders.

faq.q: What is a common external tariff?
faq.a: It is a single set of tariffs that all member countries of a bloc charge to goods coming from outside the bloc.
asks: Does every country in a customs union charge the same tax?
What is the CET used for?

facts: FTAs aim to reduce trade barriers between signatory countries.
A customs union requires members to adopt a Common External Tariff.
The WTO aims to ensure trade flows as smoothly and predictably as possible.
Globalisation increases the interdependence of national economies.

quiz.say: A group of countries removes tariffs only between themselves but keeps separate tariffs for outside goods. This is best described as a:
quiz.why: An FTA only requires internal tariff reduction, which matches the description.

wrong.0: This term is too general; the specific mechanism is needed.
wrong.2: A customs union requires a common external tariff, which is a stronger requirement.
wrong.3: WTO membership is about adhering to global rules, not just internal tariff changes.

quiz.say: If Country X and Country Y form a customs union, what must they agree upon regarding goods from Country Z?

options.show: They must eliminate all tariffs globally.
options.say: They must eliminate all tariffs globally.

options.show: They must use the lowest tariff rate.
options.say: They must use the lowest tariff rate.

options.show: They can set separate tariffs for Country Z.
options.say: They can set separate tariffs for Country Z.

quiz.why: The core feature of a customs union is the common external tariff applied to all non-member goods.

wrong.0: They only need to harmonize tariffs on goods from outside the bloc.
wrong.2: They must use the same rate, not necessarily the lowest possible rate.
wrong.3: Setting separate tariffs would violate the 'common' aspect of the union.

quiz.say: Which concept best describes the increasing connection of economies worldwide through trade?
quiz.why: Globalisation is the broad term describing the increasing worldwide economic integration.

wrong.1: An FTA is a specific tool used to achieve globalisation, not the concept itself.
wrong.2: This is a specific type of trade agreement, too narrow for the overall concept.
wrong.3: The WTO is an institution that manages the process, not the process itself.
